profile.offer: Fractional data team for mid-market e-commerce brands: dashboards, forecasting and attribution set up in 30 days, then run monthly.
profile.audience: VPs and Directors of Ecommerce, Marketing and Finance at DTC brands doing $10M-$150M revenue.
profile.voice: Plainspoken, warm, a little dry. First names. Short sentences. No hype words, no exclamation marks, never 'just following up'.
profile.signature:
Jamie Lee
Founder, Northwind Analytics
northwind.example.com

assets.title: Northwind One Sheet
assets.description: One page: what we do, the 30-day setup, pricing tiers, three client logos.
assets.whenToUse: Prospect asks for more info, an overview, or 'send me something'.

assets.title: 2026 DTC Metrics Benchmark Report
assets.description: Benchmarks for CAC, repeat rate and contribution margin across 140 DTC brands, by revenue band.
assets.whenToUse: Prospect is curious but not ready to talk, or says 'not now'. A useful give with no ask.

assets.title: Apparel Brand Tear Sheet
assets.description: One-page result: $42M apparel brand cut blended CAC 18% in two quarters after attribution rebuild.
assets.whenToUse: Prospect is skeptical, already has a vendor/agency, or asks for proof.

assets.title: Forecasting Case Study
assets.description: Two-page case study: inventory forecasting for a $90M home goods brand, 31% fewer stockouts.
assets.whenToUse: Prospect mentions inventory, planning, or finance is the main stakeholder.

templates.name: Send info + soft ask
templates.body:
Thanks {{first_name}}. Here's the one-pager: {{asset_link}}

The short version: we set up dashboards, forecasting and attribution in about 30 days, then run it monthly. If it looks relevant, happy to walk through how it'd work for {{company}} — 20 minutes: {{calendar_link}}

templates.name: Book the call
templates.body:
Great, {{first_name}}. Here's my calendar if it's easiest to grab a time: {{calendar_link}}

If you'd rather, send me two times that work and I'll send the invite.

templates.name: Not now: give value, no ask
templates.body:
Totally fair, {{first_name}}. In the meantime this might be useful — benchmarks from 140 DTC brands, broken out by revenue band: {{asset_link}}

I'll check back in {{timeframe}}.

templates.name: Ask for the intro
templates.body: Appreciate it, {{first_name}}. Would you be open to pointing me to {{referral_name}}, or would you rather I reach out and mention you suggested it?

templates.name: Already has a vendor: proof, not pitch
templates.body: Makes sense, {{first_name}}. Not trying to replace anyone. A lot of our clients came to us after an agency setup, usually because attribution didn't match the P&L. Here's one example in case it's ever useful: {{asset_link}}

templates.name: Polite close
templates.body: Understood, {{first_name}}, thanks for letting me know. Wishing you a strong Q4.

templates.name: Email: send info

matrix.goal: Give them the right one-pager and make booking a call the obvious next step.

options.label: Send the one sheet + soft call ask
Send proof that matches their situation
options.guidance: Use when they are in apparel or mention CAC/attribution.

options.label: Email version (if they gave an email)

matrix.avoid: Do not paste the whole pitch into the message. Do not send more than two assets.

matrix.goal: Get a time on the calendar with as little back-and-forth as possible.

options.label: Calendar link + one sheet to review beforehand
options.guidance: Use when they seem to want context before the call.

matrix.avoid: No more selling. They said yes.

matrix.goal: Leave a useful asset, set a specific follow-up time, keep the door open.

options.label: Send the benchmark report, check back later
options.guidance: Use the timeframe they gave; if none, say 'early next quarter'.

matrix.avoid: Do not push for a call.

matrix.scenario: Objection: already have a vendor / in-house team
matrix.goal: Plant a seed with proof without arguing.

options.label: Give the benchmark report as a free check
options.guidance: Frame it as a way to sanity-check their current numbers.

matrix.goal: Get the name and, ideally, a warm intro.
Give a straight answer (the one sheet has tiers) and offer to scope it on a call.

options.label: Point to tiers in the one sheet + offer to scope
options.guidance: Mention that pricing tiers are on the one sheet. Do not quote numbers that aren't in the background knowledge.

matrix.goal: Close gracefully. If they asked to stop, confirm and stop.
Don't reply now; note the return date and follow up after it.

options.label: No reply now: follow up after their return date
options.guidance: Draft a short message for after they return and say when to send it.

knowledge.title: Pricing and packaging notes
knowledge.text: Three tiers: Starter (dashboards only), Growth (dashboards + attribution), Full (adds forecasting). Setup is a fixed 30-day project, then monthly retainer. Exact pricing is shared on the call, not in DMs.
